hints: Focus on splitting the ester at the middle oxygen of the COO group, since acid hydrolysis reverses ester formation.
Notice the left part $(CH_3)_2CH O$ has three carbons with the O on the middle carbon, so think which propanol that makes.
Count the carbons on the right part $CO(CH_2)_2CH_3$ including the $C=O$ carbon to work out the length of the carboxylic acid.
walkthrough:
**Recall acid hydrolysis of esters**

Boiling an ester with aqueous acid splits it back into its parent parts. Think of it as adding water across the ester link.

$$RCOOR' + H_2O \rightarrow RCOOH + R'OH$$

**Split the given ester**

Write the ester as two halves around the central O. The alcohol part comes from the left, the acid part comes from the right.

$$ (CH_3)_2CH O \text{ } | \text{ } CO(CH_2)_2CH_3 $$
Left gives $(CH_3)_2CHOH$, right gives $HOCO(CH_2)_2CH_3$.

**Identify the alcohol**

The left fragment $(CH_3)_2CHOH$ is $CH_3CH(OH)CH_3$. The OH is on carbon 2 of a 3-carbon chain, so this is propan-2-ol, not propan-1-ol.

**Identify the carboxylic acid**

The right fragment is $CH_3CH_2CH_2COOH$. Count carefully: the $C=O$ carbon plus $(CH_2)_2$ plus $CH_3$ gives 4 carbons in total, so this is butanoic acid.

options.A: Propan-1-ol is wrong. The alcohol fragment is $(CH_3)_2CHOH$ with OH on the middle carbon, which is propan-2-ol. Butanoic acid is correct for the acid part.
options.B: This is correct. Acid hydrolysis gives $(CH_3)_2CHOH$ which is propan-2-ol, and $CH_3CH_2CH_2COOH$ which is butanoic acid with 4 carbons.
options.C: Both parts are miscounted. The alcohol is secondary, not primary, so not propan-1-ol. The acid has 4 carbons including the carbonyl carbon, so not propanoic acid which has only 3.
options.D: Propan-2-ol is correct, but propanoic acid is wrong. Students who forget to count the $C=O$ carbon get 3 carbons instead of 4 and choose propanoic acid instead of butanoic acid.
